1.w: Wine is a mocker and strong drink is a brawler; whoever goes astray by them is not wise.

2.w: The king’s terrifying anger is like the roar of a lion; whoever provokes him sins against himself.

3.w: It is an honor for a person to cease from strife, but every fool quarrels.

4.w: The sluggard will not plow during the planting season, so at harvest time he asks for grain but has nothing.

5.w: Counsel in a person’s heart is like deep water, but an understanding person draws it out.

6.w: Many people profess their loyalty, but a faithful person —who can find?

7.w: The righteous person behaves in integrity; blessed are his children after him.

8.w: A king sitting on the throne to judge separates out all evil with his eyes.

9.w: Who can say, “I have kept my heart clean; I am pure from my sin”?

10.w: Diverse weights and diverse measures — the Lord abhors both of them.

11.w: Even a young man is known by his actions, whether his activity is pure and whether it is right.

12.w: The ear that hears and the eye that sees — the Lord has made them both.

13.w: Do not love sleep, lest you become impoverished; open your eyes so that you might be satisfied with food.

14.w: “It’s worthless! It’s worthless!” says the buyer, but when he goes on his way, he boasts.

15.w: There is gold and an abundance of rubies, but words of knowledge are like a precious jewel.

16.w: Take a man’s garment when he has given security for a stranger, and hold him in pledge on behalf of strangers.

17.w: Bread gained by deceit tastes sweet to a person, but afterward his mouth will be filled with gravel.

18.w: Plans are established by counsel, so make war with guidance.

19.w: The one who goes about gossiping reveals secrets; therefore do not associate with someone who is always opening his mouth.

20.w: The one who curses his father and his mother, his lamp will be extinguished in the blackest darkness.

21.w: An inheritance gained easily in the beginning will not be blessed in the end.

22.w: Do not say, “I will pay back evil!” Wait for the Lord, so that he may vindicate you.

23.w: The Lord abhors differing weights, and dishonest scales are wicked.

24.w: The steps of a person are ordained by the Lord— so how can anyone understand his own way?

25.w: It is a snare for a person to rashly cry, “Holy!” and only afterward to consider what he has vowed.

26.w: A wise king separates out the wicked; he turns the threshing wheel over them.

27.w: The human spirit is like the lamp of the Lord, searching all his innermost parts.

28.w: Loyal love and truth preserve a king, and his throne is upheld by loyal love.

29.w: The glory of young men is their strength, and the splendor of old men is gray hair.

30.w: Beatings and wounds cleanse away evil, and floggings cleanse the innermost being.
